answer: Practically, the chain should mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because orchard only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, atlas is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any hollow approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
